newsitem.title: USA: Campbell posts record profits, sales.
newsitem.headline: Campbell posts record profits, sales.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co. Wednesday posted record profits and sales for its fiscal third quarter, led by a 15 percent increase in worldwide sales of its soups.

Campbell, which also marketsGoldfish snack crackers andGodiva chocolates, said its net income for the three months ended April 27 grew 8 percent to a record $157 million, or 34 cents a share, from $145 million, or 29 cents a share.
Wall Street reacted positively to the news, sending Campbell's stock up $1.375 to $49.375 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The earnings per share reflected a 2-for-1 stock split in March and Campbell's share buyback programme, under which the company bought 4.7 million shares in the quarter, bringing the nine-month total to 35.6 million shares, or $1.5 billion.
The company said its net sales for the quarter rose 2 percent to a record $1.87 billion from $1.83 billion last year. Excluding divestitures, sales from ongoing businesses increased 5 percent.

"Our robust global soup sales attest to the strength of our 'Best in Show' strategic growth plan," Chairman David W. Johnson said in a statement. "Our innovation meter is running at full tilt. New products likeJoseph A. Campbell premium soup in glass andCampbell's 98 percent fat-free cream soups are 'hot.'"

The company said its net income for the first nine months of its fiscal year fell 16 percent to $521 million, or $1.09 a share, from $621 million, or $1.25 a share, as it took a $216 million charge for restructuring.
Sales for the nine months increased 3 percent to $6.24 billion from $6.04 billion last year.
"One of the greatest strengths of Campbell Soup Company is the tremendous capacity of our low cost business systems to deliver steady margin improvement," said Johnson, who is also president and CEO.

"The combination of continued productivity gains, improved business mix and pricing flexibility on our core brands has raised our gross margin to 44.9 percent from 42.0 percent for the same quarter a year ago."
Campbell, based in Camden, N.J., said its U.S. sales slipped 2 percent to $1.08 billion from $1.09 billion due to divestitures.
Before divestitures, its said, U.S. sales rose 3 percent while operating earnings increased 12 percent to $227 million.

The company said sales at its confectionary division, which sells Goldfish crackers, Milano cookies and Godiva chocolate, expanded by 5 percent while sales at its international grocery unit expanded by 11 percent.
Campbell said the international sales gain was led by Erasco, Germany's leading soup company, which was acquired in September.
